issue: The spec says to reject any member whose parent path crosses an archive symlink. `_refuse_duplicate_or_crossing_members` rejects only a crossing that `_land` resolves to an escape, a `..` past the root, an absolute target or a cycle. A file under a symlink that stays inside the tree is accepted. Safe internal links are a stated "preserve" item, so this reading is arguable, but it is looser than the written rule. The tests encode the looser rule, and no test pins the strict reading or its relaxation.
reason: single-voice. Not dismissed on merit: this is the same defect as R8, raised independently by Blake and Bob in wording the consolidator did not merge (cited at trees.py:141 and :142), so its true consensus is 2/3. The substance is carried into R4's fix task, which names it explicitly

issue: Duplicate detection uses `posixpath.normpath` on the raw name. It does not fold case or Unicode, so two names that collide on a case-insensitive filesystem (macOS default) pass the preflight. On the compatibility path nothing else catches this, and the data filter does not catch it either. Two entries such as `Escape` as a link and `escape/x` as a file, which the preflight sees as unrelated, can still alias on such a host.
reason: single-voice. Nobody executed the claimed collision, so it stands as an unverified bypass vector on a case-insensitive host. Re-raise with a demonstrated case if it recurs

issue: `_land` permits members beneath safe symlinks, contrary to the PRD's ancestor-crossing refusal requirement. With `alias -> pkg`, `alias/file` can overwrite `pkg/file` despite distinct normalized names. Explicitly reject symlink ancestors and test this alias collision.
reason: single-voice. Same defect as R6 (see that entry); the substance is carried into R4's fix task
